name: og-ecology
primary_limitation: The community function is productivity, not robustness - under low-count demographic noise the community is ~2x more variable than monoculture; the model is a lightweight reproduction (Option B), not a wrapped ALife engine.
key_assumptions: Community dynamics are an exact numpy Gillespie SSA with a matched mean-field ODE (Option B)
Cross-feeding and coexistence are stabilized, not assumed
title: Protocell Ecology: Does Community Function Precede the Cell?
concept: Whether protocell-era chemistry is ecological before it is cellular — a cross-feeding community that out-produces the best single lineage and whose function precedes cell completeness — one concept (Gate E), studied at several fidelities as arms: the stochastic community-vs-single-lineage gate (og-36), the connected metacommunity (og-07), and real metabolite exchange (og-07-alt).
gate_reason: Gate E (optional extension), ecology. This consolidates the ecology line into one concept with explicit arms, each judged against its own matched null with input fluxes held equal: the stochastic community-vs-best-single gate (og-36, canonical), the connected-vs-isolated metacommunity (og-07), and real metabolite-exchange community function (og-07-alt). Headline is bounded by the most-caveated arm: QUALIFIED — a cross-feeding community out-produces the best single lineage with a causally-cross-feeding margin and function that precedes cell completeness, but it is NOT more robust than monoculture and low-count stochasticity materially changes outcomes. Each arm keeps its own verdict and matched null (see arms).
claim: Protocell-era chemistry is ecological before it is cellular. A stochastic cross-feeding community out-produces the best single lineage with the margin causally attributable to cross-feeding and coexistence stabilized (not assumed), though the community is NOT more robust than monoculture and low-count stochasticity materially changes outcomes (og-36, qualified); a connected metacommunity beats an isolated control with cross-feeding robustness and closed ledgers (og-07, supported); and real metabolite exchange makes community function PRECEDE cell completeness and VANISH without exchange, segregated placement keeping function (og-07-alt, supported). Headline verdict qualified; every matched null and every arm verdict preserved.
question: Is protocell-era chemistry ecological before it is cellular — does a cross-feeding community out-produce the best single lineage (margin causally cross-feeding), does community function precede cell completeness and vanish without exchange — each against its own matched null with input fluxes held equal?
hypothesis: A cross-feeding community out-produces the best single lineage and sustains a function no single lineage performs, with the benefit causal to exchange and coexistence stabilized rather than assumed; where the community is not more robust, or stochasticity changes low-count outcomes, that is reported honestly rather than tuned to a pass.
experiment: Run the stochastic community-vs-best-single composite against a matched equal-feed null (og-36), the connected-vs-isolated metacommunity (og-07), and the real metabolite-exchange community against a no-exchange/count-only null (og-07-alt) — reporting each arm's verdict + matched null with element ledgers closed and the stochastic / robustness caveats stated plainly.

provides: productivity margin over best single lineage

arms.concept_role: Canonical arm (Gate E, plan 36): under stochastic low-count dynamics does a cross-feeding community out-produce the best single lineage, with coexistence stabilized (not assumed) and the margin causally cross-feeding, vs a matched equal-feed null? Realized: qualified — community out-produces best single and the margin is causally cross-feeding, but the community is NOT more robust than monoculture and stochasticity materially changes low-count outcomes.

Metacommunity arm: before any complete cell, does a connected cross-feeding metacommunity beat an isolated control (cross-feeding robustness, LUCA-capability overlap), element ledger closed? Realized: supported — connected beats isolated, cross-feeding robust, ledgers close.

Real-metabolite-exchange arm: does community function (a shared reductive branch) PRECEDE cell completeness and VANISH without metabolite exchange, vs a no-exchange / count-only null? Realized: supported — community function precedes cell completeness, is flux-sustained, and vanishes without exchange; segregated placement keeps function; map ledgers close.

findings.evidence_basis_note: Cross-feeding community output at equal shared feed is an SSA model result, not fit.
findings.statement: At equal shared feed, the SSA cross-feeding community out-produces the BEST single lineage by ~1.9x (community 1522 vs best-single 812 cumulative births; margin 710, positive in 100% of 24 seeds), and the margin is CAUSALLY cross-feeding - a knockout at equal feed collapses it to 11 (~2% of the community margin). Coexistence is stabilised by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), not assumed: deterministically all 4 lineages persist (n_alive 4), the knockout excludes down (n_alive 2). So an emergent community function exists and is cross-feeding-caused, not mere diversity.

The community function is productivity, NOT robustness. Under low-count demographic noise the community is ~2x more variable than the monoculture (CV 0.085 vs 0.037) and loses a lineage in ~12% of runs, and a system-size (Omega) sweep shows this divergence from the deterministic mean-field GROWING as counts fall (Omega 0.7: 31% extinction, 20% margin erosion; Omega >= 2: effectively deterministic); the mean-field misses the lineage loss entirely. So the ecology RAISES productivity but PAYS in robustness — the COUNTERPOINT to Gate B (pore), Gate C (membrane) and Gate E/35 (energy carrier), each of which bought persistence/robustness but NOT throughput. Across all four gates robustness is the consistently traded axis. A community that were both more robust and more productive would be a cleaner result; buying one by spending the other is the honest qualified verdict.

Model is Option B - a lightweight dependency-free numpy Gillespie SSA (exact) with a matched mean-field ODE, honestly a reproduction, not a wrapped ALife engine; parameters are labelled proposed_inputs, not fitted. The GillesPy2 / SSA tau-leaping engine and a COBRApy genome-scale metabolic benchmark - which would re-test the cross-feeding community function under resolved, genome-scale chemistry - are the gold-standard follow-on (og-36a).

findings.evidence_basis_note: Connected-vs-isolated robustness gain across 8 seeds is a model outcome.
findings.statement: A connected metacommunity of 8 pore compartments, each carrying a sparse coarse-grained protometabolic capability vector (2 of 12 functions intrinsic), develops functional redundancy (robustness 0.667) through cross-feeding and horizontal transfer, well above the isolated counterfactual (0.500) run on the identical seeded assignment. Across an 8-seed sweep the connected arm (0.71±0.08) strictly beats the isolated arm (0.42±0.06) on every seed (min gain 0.17), so the redundancy is a product of connectivity, not of the capability assignment.

evidence.observed: connected robustness 0.71±0.08 vs isolated 0.42±0.06 across 8 seeds, 8/8 pass, min gain 0.17

findings.explanation: Coarse-grained deterministic metacommunity (reproduction, not wrapped ALife). Cross-feeding (a compartment expressing a capability its neighbour lacks supplies the byproduct) and horizontal transfer (the capability is copied from a donor) spread sparse intrinsic capabilities into redundant coverage across the ring; a capability held by >= 2 compartments survives a single-compartment loss. Acquired capability decays toward the intrinsic set, so it persists only while continuously supplied.

findings.statement: Robustness EMERGES only in a bounded corner of (cross-feeding exchange_rate x inter-compartment diversity). At low diversity the compartments are near-identical, so cross-feeding/HGT have nothing to share and robustness stays at the sparse intrinsic floor (~0.17-0.25 regardless of exchange); at low exchange a diverse-but-disconnected set holds a broad repertoire fragilely (each capability in one compartment, ~0.33-0.42); only where diversity >= ~0.4 AND exchange crosses ~0.2 does robustness climb to 0.58-0.83. The transition is a phase boundary, not a monotone response to either knob alone. The companion three-view Decision map over (exchange_rate x parasite_load) at the canonical diversity sharpens this — robustness clears the 0.5 emergence boundary only once exchange crosses ~0.2 AND parasite load stays low (0.667 at the parasite-free operating point), collapsing toward 0 as parasites drain their neighbours.

evidence.observed: robustness landscape over (exchange x diversity): emergence boundary at exchange~0.2, diversity~0.4; companion (exchange x parasite_load) Decision map clears 0.5 only in the well-connected, low-parasite corner; canonical operating point 0.667 (auto-graded gate 0.646)

findings.explanation: Cross-feeding scales as exchange_rate/connectivity and is deficit-driven (zero between identical compartments), so diversity is the raw material and exchange is the spreading mechanism; both are necessary. The sparse capability space (2 of 12 intrinsic per compartment) makes an isolated compartment functionally fragile, so redundancy must be BUILT by the metacommunity.

findings.statement: The metacommunity's collective capability repertoire overlaps the Weiss-2016 anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA core at 0.60 (canonical) and 0.70±0.14 across seeds. This is reported as a far-end BOUNDARY the emergent set approaches from below — a phylogenomic constraint on capabilities eventually acquired — and is explicitly NOT a fitting target; the model is never tuned toward it.

evidence.observed: collective LUCA-core overlap 0.60 canonical, 0.70±0.14 across 8 seeds (reported, not gated)

findings.explanation: The LUCA reconstruction (anaerobic, H2-dependent, CO2-fixing, FeS-rich; Weiss 2016, 355 protein families; Moody 2024, LUCA embedded in an ecosystem ~4.2 Ga) is a constraint on which capabilities the lineage eventually acquired, used as a boundary condition on the emergent repertoire rather than as evidence the first compartments were LUCA-like.

findings.statement: The community of a carboxylating and a hydrogenating lineage holds malate (c4_diacid_hydroxy) at 6.4e-9 M in its reducer agents although the fixer monoculture, the reducer monoculture and the private (no-sharing) arm hold 0 M and neither monoculture ever produces it; the generalist (complete-cell) arm holds 1.36e-7 M, so the community reaches 4.7 % of a complete cell (3.9e-3 vs 0.08 molecules per 1-fL agent: a mean-field occupancy). The best agent in the community holds 14 of the 15 product classes in the union (max completeness 0.933, mean 0.867), so the function is present while no cell is complete.

evidence.observed: 1 community-only class (c4_diacid_hydroxy); levels community 6.4e-9 / mono 0 / private 0 / generalist 1.4e-7 M; max completeness 0.933

findings.explanation: The fixer's carboxylate_alpha rule makes oxaloacetate from pyruvate + CO2 (gross 5e-6 M/s) but the fixer has no reduction rule; the reducer's reduce_carbonyl rule turns oxaloacetate + H2 into malate but the reducer has no carboxylation rule. Both lineages are the same universe with 413 reversible reactions, eQuilibrator dG' and detailed balance; only the 0/1 rule mask differs. Artifact: artifacts/community_function_map.json (gate.levels, gate.max_cell_completeness).

findings.statement: The community-only function vanishes when nothing is shared (private arm: each agent exchanges only with its own copy of the background; malate 0 M) and its precursor oxaloacetate — a species the reducer cannot make in monoculture — crosses between the lineages at 1.8e-27 mol per tick (1.1e-3 molecules per tick over the 8 agents), while formate (1.7e-24) and lactate (3.6e-25 mol/tick) carry the largest cross-lineage fluxes. The exchange rules fired 468,331 times on the canonical run (secretion 135,316, uptake 115,466, pore diffusion 93,009, feed / washout 124,540); no rule moves a capability.

evidence.observed: vanish without exchange 1/1; precursor oxaloacetate 1.1e-3 molecules/tick; firings 468,331

findings.explanation: The SpatialCouplingStep's BigraphicalReactiveSystem moves only matter, as the exact two-compartment relaxation of each species through a size- and charge-dependent permeability (same float out of one place, into the other); the cross-lineage flux is the moles a species was secreted by one lineage and taken up by another in the same tick. Artifact: artifacts/community_function_map.json (gate.precursors, gate.vanish_without_exchange, ledger.firings_by_rule_nominal_community).

findings.statement: Over (diacid permeability x pore residence) the community-only function appears from 3e-9 m/s at 20 s and 100 s residence (malate 1.1e-9 / 1.5e-9 M at the boundary, 2.0e-8 M at 1e-7 m/s and 100 s) and only at 1e-7 m/s at 500 s residence, where the shared feed is depleted; below 3e-9 m/s the dicarboxylate decarboxylates back to pyruvate inside the fixer before it can cross. The measured permeability of charged solutes through fatty-acid vesicles (~1e-11-1e-10 m/s) lies 1-2 decades below the boundary.

evidence.observed: emergence at p_diacid = 3e-9 m/s (residence 20, 100 s), 1e-7 m/s (500 s); 21 points x 4 arms

findings.explanation: The membrane rate constant k = P A / V competes with oxaloacetate's thermal beta-decarboxylation (0.02/s) and with the pore washout; the Decision map is the region where k wins. The diacid permeability is hypothetical in vg-data cnp_resources (the weakest number) and is swept, not asserted; the measured anchor is proposed in the investigation's proposed_inputs (pending). Artifact: artifacts/community_function_map.json (decision_map).

findings.statement: og-07's gate readouts recomputed from the agents map (capabilities = product classes held by >= 2 agents): metacommunity robustness 0.54 in the shared community vs 0.46 in the private arm, 0.25 / 0.32 in the monocultures and 0.68 for complete cells; capability diversity 0.46 vs 0.29 (private); LUCA-core overlap 0.8 for every arm with a fixer (H2 oxidation, CO2 fixation, FeS-type catalysis and acetate are realised; ion pumping is unreachable in a C/H/O network), 0.6 for the reducer alone. The within-run isolated counterfactual (functions an agent PRODUCES) equals the held robustness, so og-07's "acquired capability" has no counterpart in real chemistry: what an agent acquires by flux is a precursor, and the function it then performs is its own.
findings.explanation: The EcologyReducerStep keeps og-07's names (metacommunity_robustness, isolated_robustness, robustness_gain, capability_diversity, luca_capability_overlap, mean_capability) and reads them off real pools and real fluxes; the connected-vs-isolated comparison therefore moves from a within-process counterfactual to the private arm. Artifact: artifacts/community_function_map.json (og07).

findings.statement: The reaction-universe matched null (degree-preserving, (C,O)-matched rewiring) inside every agent with the same rule masks yields 0 (seed 0) and 1 (seed 1: c1_methanol, 2.5e-8 M, absent in its own private arm) community-only classes, so a rule partition can split a pathway across lineages in rewired chemistry too; what the real universe adds is that the split function is the reductive C4 branch of carbon fixation. Segregating the lineages into separate pore blocks keeps the function (1 community-only class) because pore diffusion (k_diffusion 0.1/s, hypothetical) carries the intermediate between cells.

evidence.observed: null community-only classes 0 / 1 over two rewiring seeds; segregated placement 1

findings.explanation: Reported, not gated: the gate is existence of a flux-sustained community function in the real universe; the null count bounds how much of that is the partition rather than the chemistry. Artifact: artifacts/community_function_map.json (null, segregated).

findings.statement: The cross-system element ledger — C, N and P summed over every agent's interior and every field cell against the pore inflow, washout and the carbon degraded to tar — closes on all 98 runs: C residual <= 6.5e-9 (the agents' CVODE tolerance), N <= 1.1e-15 and P <= 1.4e-15 (round-off: no rule transforms them). The vg-data package cnp_resources carries 23 parameters: 0 measured, 2 calibrated (the vent carbon feed), 7 inferred, 7 extrapolated, 7 hypothetical (the diacid permeability, the C:N:P demand, the pore cells and diffusion), none unsourced.

evidence.observed: C residual max 6.5e-9, N 1.1e-15, P 1.4e-15 on 98 runs; audit 0/2/7/7/7, unsourced []

findings.explanation: The honesty indicator; the headline permeability boundary rests on the one hypothetical class and the measured anchor is pending.

config.title: Stochastic protocell ecology — productivity, not robustness
Connected vs disconnected compartments (matched diversity & budgets)
config.caption: Exchange among heterogeneous pore compartments can increase functional redundancy, subject to cross-feeding and parasite-load tradeoffs. Reduced to the one mechanistic comparison — connected vs disconnected compartments at matched inter-compartment diversity and equal resource budgets. Functional breadth, functional redundancy and parasite load are distinct measures with distinct units; robustness is not inferred from richness alone.

config.title: Robustness gain over the isolated baseline
config.caption: Robustness gain over isolated compartments occupies a restricted exchange-rate × inter-compartment-diversity region. The claim is the gain over a matched isolated baseline, not richness: robustness here is functional redundancy, distinct in units from functional breadth and parasite load. The parasite regime is shown explicitly (gain erodes as parasite load rises), the modeled transfer is metabolite cross-feeding (with a horizontal channel), not heritable material, and replicate variation across stochastic seeds is included.

derived.insight: At equal shared feed, the SSA cross-feeding community out-produces the BEST single lineage by ~1.9x (community 1522 vs best-single 812 cumulative births; margin 710, positive in 100% of 24 seeds), and the margin is CAUSALLY cross-feeding - a knockout at equal feed collapses it to 11 (~2% of the community margin). Coexistence is stabilised by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), not assumed: deterministically all 4 lineages persist (n_alive 4), the knockout excludes down (n_alive 2). So an emergent community function exists and is cross-feeding-caused, not mere diversity.
